content.value_statement: Agent systems often fail when context grows without structure or budget discipline. This skill teaches context components, attention limits, progressive disclosure, and practical budgeting patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains core context components, including system prompts, tool definitions, documents, message history, and tool outputs.
Describes attention limits, position effects, and why long context can reduce precision.
Provides guidance for progressive disclosure, document loading, and context budgeting.
Includes examples for structured system prompts and staged document loading.
Supplies Python utilities for token estimation, context building, truncation, validation, and progressive disclosure.
limitations: Token counting utilities use rough estimates and are not a replacement for provider tokenizers.
The skill teaches concepts and patterns; it does not integrate with live model APIs.
Examples are generic and require adaptation for each agent stack.
It does not automatically enforce context budgets in production systems.

use_cases.title: Design Agent Context Flows
use_cases.description: Plan what context loads at startup, on demand, and after compaction.

use_cases.title: Debug Context Failures
use_cases.description: Identify missed instructions, bloated history, weak retrieval, or excessive tool output.

use_cases.title: Teach Context Engineering
use_cases.description: Use the reference material to onboard teams to context windows, attention limits, and progressive disclosure.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My Context Stack
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an agent design
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the five main context components for my agent: system prompt, tools, documents, history, and tool outputs. Use one risk and one improvement for each.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Context Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent design and identify where context may become too large or low signal. Suggest a smaller context plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Progressive Disclosure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for large reference sets
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a progressive disclosure plan for a documentation-heavy agent. Specify what loads at startup, what loads on demand, and when to compact.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test Degradation
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this long-running agent workflow for context degradation. Define warning thresholds, compaction triggers, and recovery steps for missed details.

output_examples.input: Review an agent that preloads all API documentation before every task.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend loading a short API summary first, then retrieving endpoint and authentication details only when needed.

output_examples.input: Explain why a model missed instructions in the middle of a long conversation.
output_examples.output: The skill would point to attention distribution, message history growth, and the need to place critical instructions near favored positions.

output_examples.input: Create a context budget for a support agent with tools and documents.
output_examples.output: The skill would divide budget across system instructions, tool definitions, recent messages, retrieved documents, and compact tool outputs.

best_practices: Start with the smallest high-signal context that can solve the current task.
Keep critical instructions near attention-favored positions and repeat only essential constraints.
Use summaries, references, and on-demand loading before expanding full context.
anti_patterns: Preloading every document because the model has a large context window.
Splitting documents at fixed character counts without preserving semantic boundaries.
Treating compaction as an emergency step instead of a planned workflow.

faq.question: What is context engineering?
faq.answer: It is the practice of selecting, organizing, and limiting the information available to an AI model.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when designing agents, debugging context failures, reducing token usage, or teaching context fundamentals.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other agents with finite context windows.

faq.question: Does this skill call external services?
faq.answer: No. The included material is local documentation and example Python utilities.

faq.question: Are the included scripts production-ready?
faq.answer: No. They provide simple examples and rough estimates that need provider tokenizers for production use.

faq.question: Can this reduce token costs?
faq.answer: Yes. Progressive disclosure and context budgeting can reduce unnecessary tokens while preserving task-relevant information.
